title: A Concise Bounded Description
description: An Instance with its Work embedded, and with the resources they name described in place: enough in one document to explain the Instance without fetching anything.
$comment:
cbd-01.md is LC's description of how they serialize a CBD, and it describes RDF/XML: all principal resources as siblings under one rdf:RDF, linked by rdf:resource. That arrangement suits XML, where there is no natural root, and Marva reads it.

JSON has a natural root, and LC never specified the JSON-LD -- their .cbd.jsonld is a flat array of expanded nodes, and Blue Core's was the same. So this takes the other option: the document is the Instance, and everything else is described where it is referenced. Measured over 59 CBDs from a running system it is 11% smaller than the sibling arrangement and describes exactly the same resources, and it puts a related Work where it belongs -- under the relation that reaches it -- rather than leaving a reader to rejoin URIs.

The one structural claim, and the thing that tells a CBD from a stored record: bf:instanceOf embeds the Work. In a stored record it is a bare URI, because the Work is a row of its own. The back-reference from the embedded Work is still bare, which is how a JSON-LD processor breaks the cycle and is what dialect.json already permits.

Everything else is dialect.json, referenced rather than copied so the definitions exist in one place.

instance-at-the-root.title: The document is an Instance
instance-at-the-root.description: A CBD is bounded by one Instance. Blue Core serves one for an Instance and nothing else; a Hub is described by the 'decomposed' form, which is a different document.

work-embedded.title: With its Work embedded
work-embedded.description: Not a bare URI, which is what a stored record holds. This is the difference between the two, and the reason a CBD is self-explaining.
work-embedded.$comment: The embedded Work is checked by dialect.json as a resource, not merely as a reference. Without that it is only checked as a reference -- which is open, so a blank node keeping its @id inside the Work would pass. The sibling arrangement got this for free, because every member was dispatched as a resource; nesting has to ask for it.
